entries.name: Excel MCP server (live COM, .NET) — Click-to-Run / Microsoft 365
entries.summary: Automate Microsoft Excel through its native COM API — Power Query, DAX measures, PivotTables, charts, formatting, and VBA macros (25 tools / ~230 operations) with real recalc against the live Excel process. Community server sbroenne/mcp-server-excel (C#/.NET 10), pinned to release v1.8.70. Distributed as a self-contained mcp-excel.exe — download from the release ZIP and add to PATH (see vendored_source.install_cmd); the launch command is the bare `mcp-excel` binary, not uvx. disabled-until-probe: enables only when Excel AND the mcp-excel server binary are present. PROBE SCOPE: this row targets a Click-to-Run / Microsoft 365 Excel install (the C:\Program Files*\Microsoft Office\root\Office1?\EXCEL.EXE layout, where the `root\` segment is the Click-to-Run signature). MSI / volume-license installs lay EXCEL.EXE down WITHOUT the `root\` segment (…\Microsoft Office\Office16\EXCEL.EXE), so the host-detect probe does NOT cover them in this batch — filepath.Glob has no `**` and the install_probe uses AND-semantics across entries, so it cannot OR the optional `root\` across two patterns. A file_globs[] OR-group probe model covering Click-to-Run + MSI + macOS is the tracked D-3 follow-up. The VBA-exec / RunMacro operations execute arbitrary code in the live workbook — gate the 6 VBA-exec ops behind operator consent (D-4). Windows + Click-to-Run Excel desktop only.

vendored_source.install_cmd: download mcp-excel.exe from the v1.8.70 release ZIP (https://github.com/sbroenne/mcp-server-excel/releases/tag/v1.8.70), extract to a tools dir, and add that dir to PATH

entries.name: Ableton Live MCP server (loopback-safe)
entries.summary: Control Ableton Live over a TCP socket — create/edit tracks, clips, devices, and transport via the Live Object Model. This is the loopback-safe fork applicate2628/ableton-mcp-loopback (a security fork of ahujasid/ableton-mcp, Python, MIT), pinned to an immutable commit and run via uvx from that git source. PROVENANCE: the fork is a focused security+hardening fork — vs upstream it changes the bind to loopback, removes telemetry, and adds NDJSON socket framing, pre-LOM input validation, socket I/O-locking, and finite timeouts + bounded thread cleanup; full tool parity is preserved. It is security-reviewed (independent security gate + deep-review APPROVED). The row pins this reviewed SOURCE commit for the uvx-run MCP server, AND the manually-installed Remote Script must be taken from the SAME pinned commit (not the moving HEAD) — see SETUP. Scope of the guarantee: it covers the fork's reviewed SOURCE commit, NOT the full transitive runtime — a uvx install still resolves Python deps from PyPI (the fork declares mcp[cli]>=1.3.0, not a locked set). Upstream's MIT license + attribution are preserved. The in-Live Remote Script binds 127.0.0.1 (loopback) as a HARD CONSTANT, so Ableton control is NOT reachable from the LAN — the kernel refuses any non-loopback peer, and no firewall rule is needed. This fixes upstream ahujasid/ableton-mcp's HOST=0.0.0.0 bind (LAN-reachable). Full tool parity with upstream: tracks/clips/notes/transport/devices/browser/arrangement/audio-clip. disabled-until-probe: enables only when a SUPPORTED Ableton Live is installed. REQUIRES Ableton Live 10 or newer — upstream advertises 'Ableton Live 10 or newer' and does NOT support Live 9 or earlier; the install probe therefore narrows to Live 10-19 via the glob C:\ProgramData\Ableton\Live 1[0-9]*\Program\Ableton Live 1[0-9]*.exe (the 1[0-9] char-class matches Live 10-19 across all editions Suite/Standard/Intro/Lite and EXCLUDES Live 9 and earlier, whose version segment does not begin with '1' followed by a digit), so a host with only an unsupported pre-10 install does not falsely pass admission for a server it cannot drive. Live 20+ (when released) will need a glob update — file_globs[] entries are AND-semantics and cannot OR a second version range, so a second range is a follow-up. macOS (/Applications/Ableton Live *.app) is NOT covered in this batch — the install_probe uses AND-semantics across entries and cannot OR a second install root, so a macOS row (or file_globs[] OR-group support) is a follow-up. SETUP (operator-side, REQUIRED): install the bundled Remote Script — RemoteScript/__init__.py from the PINNED commit, not the moving HEAD (raw: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/applicate2628/ableton-mcp-loopback/12e5e8bad363d86cdffccccca266f775a5f90bbf/RemoteScript/__init__.py) — into your Ableton User Library Remote Scripts folder, then select it in Live (Preferences -> Link/Tempo/MIDI -> Control Surface). NOTE: if your Windows Documents are OneDrive-redirected, your User Library is under OneDrive\Documents\Ableton\User Library, not the plain Documents path — install there. The MCP server connects to the script over loopback TCP 9877; the host-exe probe detects Live, not the script, so verify the script is loaded before use.

entries.name: MATLAB MCP server (official, MathWorks)
entries.summary: Run MATLAB from an AI client — execute code, scripts, and functions against a live MATLAB process via the official MathWorks Go MCP server (matlab-mcp-server, stdio). OFFICIAL MathWorks server (matlab/matlab-mcp-server, pinned to release v0.11.0) — NOT a community fork, so no vendored_source (like the codex row). Distributed as a self-contained matlab-mcp-server binary: download matlab-mcp-server-windows-x64.exe from the v0.11.0 release and add it to PATH (rename to matlab-mcp-server), OR `go install github.com/matlab/matlab-mcp-server/cmd/matlab-mcp-server@latest`. REQUIRES a host MATLAB R2021a-or-later install ON THE SYSTEM PATH — by default the server finds the first MATLAB on PATH (it can also be pointed at one via --matlab-root / the MW_MCP_SERVER_MATLAB_ROOT env var, but this row sets no args/env so PATH is the only discovery), then drives the live MATLAB engine, so executing MATLAB code runs arbitrary host computation; the operator gates that the same way they gate any code-exec tool. disabled-until-probe: enables only when BOTH the matlab-mcp-server binary AND the `matlab` launcher are on PATH — the probe (binaries: matlab-mcp-server + matlab) AGREES with the server's own PATH discovery, so a MATLAB installed but NOT on PATH does not falsely enable the row. If you keep MATLAB off PATH, pass --matlab-root=<MATLAB root> (or set MW_MCP_SERVER_MATLAB_ROOT) in the manifest after install. License: MathWorks custom (BSD-style, with a clause restricting use to MathWorks products).

entries.name: Ansys MAPDL MCP server (PyMAPDL)
entries.summary: Drive Ansys MAPDL (Mechanical APDL) from an AI client through PyMAPDL — launch/connect to a MAPDL session and run finite-element analysis. Official Ansys server ansys/pymapdl-mcp (Python, FastMCP, stdio), pinned to release v0.2.1; published on PyPI as ansys-mapdl-mcp, run via uvx with the version pinned in args (like serena's pinned uvx source), so no vendored_source (official Ansys-org package, Apache-2.0). disabled-until-probe: enables only when an Ansys MAPDL install is detected via the version-agnostic glob C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v*\ansys\bin\winx64\ansys*.exe — the Ansys solver executable is itself version-stamped (ansys241.exe for 2024 R1, etc.) under a v<ver> root (v231/v241/...). REQUIRES Python + uv on PATH and a host Ansys MAPDL install — the MAPDL-launching tools (launch_mapdl_session / connect_to_mapdl / disconnect_from_mapdl) start or attach to the solver and run arbitrary APDL, so the operator gates those raw solver/run tools behind consent the same way as any code-exec surface (D-4). Windows + Ansys MAPDL desktop only in this probe.

entries.name: KiCad MCP server
entries.summary: Drive KiCad EDA from an AI client — PCB design, DRC, simulation, BOM, DFM, manufacturing — through kicad-cli and the KiCad IPC / SWIG scripting API. Community server oaslananka/kicad-mcp (Python), published to PyPI as kicad-mcp-pro, pinned to v3.14.1 and run via uvx with the version pinned in --from (vendored_source block, community fork, MIT). PRIVACY: telemetry is OFF by default (OTLP export is opt-in to an operator-supplied collector), no telemetry-disable env needed. SAFETY: remote tools are read-only by default; destructive operations (board/schematic writes, manufacturing output) require explicit operator consent. disabled-until-probe: enables when uvx is on PATH AND a host KiCad 10.x install is detected via the glob C:\Program Files\KiCad\1[0-9]*\bin\kicad-cli.exe — per the server's compatibility.yaml, kicad-mcp-pro v3.14.1 targets KiCad 10.0.x as the PRIMARY supported line (KiCad 9.x was dropped/EOL after 10.0.0; 8.x is deprecated file-level-only; 7.x unsupported), so the gate matches the 10.x-and-newer roots only. REQUIRES Python 3.13+ and uv on PATH, plus a host KiCad 10.x install. Windows + KiCad desktop only in this probe.

entries.name: Suno AI Music (AceDataCloud)
entries.summary: Local AI music generation via Suno through the AceDataCloud API — runs the official mcp-suno PyPI package locally over stdio with uvx (no hosted endpoint). 27 tools spanning music generation, lyrics, media conversion, persona management, and task queries. REQUIRES an AceDataCloud API token: sign up at https://platform.acedata.cloud and mint a token on the API documentation page, then store it in the mcphub vault as the `acedata_api_token` secret (env ACEDATACLOUD_API_TOKEN = secret:acedata_api_token). The token is a REQUIRED install gate (required_secrets) — the local mcp-suno server hard-exits (exit 1) on startup when the token is unset, so a one-click install with no token is BLOCKED at install rather than crash-looping a daemon that returns 401s.

entries.name: Onshape MCP server
entries.summary: AI-assisted access to your Onshape cloud CAD documents — create sketches, extrude/revolve/sweep/fillet parts, build construction planes, take Part Studio screenshots, export STL/STEP, and write FeatureScript over the full Onshape REST API. Community server altendky/onshape-mcp, dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT (this row uses Apache-2.0). npx-packaged: the published onshape-mcp@0.4.0 npm package is a thin Node launcher around a per-platform Rust binary, run via `npx --yes onshape-mcp@0.4.0` (version pinned). PROVENANCE: onshape-mcp@0.4.0 is SLSA-provenance-attested and OIDC-published by the maintainer (altendky); the vendored_source pin is the v0.4.0 tag SHA. CLOUD — NO HOST APP: Onshape runs in the browser/cloud, so there is no local CAD install to detect; the install_probe gates only on the npx launcher being present, NOT a host binary. AUTH (two paths): the server's `auto` mode prefers OAuth (a browser login flow it walks you through on first use — no static credentials stored) OR Basic auth via Onshape API keys. To use API keys, store them in the mcphub vault and they wire to env ONSHAPE_MCP_AUTH__ACCESS_KEY = secret:onshape_access_key + ONSHAPE_MCP_AUTH__SECRET_KEY = secret:onshape_secret_key. These are OPTIONAL (not a required_secrets install gate) because OAuth is a valid alternative and the server does not hard-exit without API keys — it enters an OAuth-pending state and waits. D-4 CAVEAT: this is a CLOUD API-key (or OAuth) integration that can WRITE to your Onshape CAD documents (create/modify parts, export); supply credentials only through the hub vault, never as plaintext. PLATFORM: the published npm ships win32-x64 + linux/darwin (x64 + arm64) binaries but NOT win32-arm64 — on a Windows ARM64 host the launcher would report unsupported-platform at startup. The install_probe now ARCH-GATES on that supported platform matrix (platforms: windows/amd64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64) in addition to the binaries:[node,npx] Node-launcher check, so on a win-arm64 host the row stays inert (greyed 'probe to enable') instead of installing and then failing at daemon spawn. STATUS: early development — offered to try; some operations work more reliably than others at this stage.

entries.name: REAPER MCP server
entries.summary: Control the REAPER DAW from an AI client — 58 tools spanning project/transport, tracks, MIDI, items, FX, mixing, mastering, rendering, and audio analysis — driven through python-reapy against the REAPER Lua/Python Object Model. Community server bonfire-systems/reaper-mcp (Python), published to PyPI as reaper-mcp-server and pinned to v0.1.1, run via uvx with the version pinned in --from (vendored_source block, community fork, MIT). SECURITY (LAN exposure — SAME risk class as the Ableton row): the MCP server itself is stdio (`mcp.run(transport="stdio")` — no network listener), BUT the python-reapy distant API it requires runs a server INSIDE REAPER that binds 0.0.0.0 (upstream python-reapy Server.__init__ → `self.bind(("0.0.0.0", port))` in reapy/tools/network/server.py — verified), so once the distant API is enabled, REAPER control is reachable from your LAN, not just localhost. Restrict the reapy port to loopback via your firewall, or only run on a trusted network. This is upstream python-reapy's bind (the hub cannot patch the operator-enabled bridge). DESTRUCTIVE WRITE SURFACE: the 58 tools can MODIFY project state and files — save projects, delete tracks/items, import audio, render stems, change FX/mix params — so a one-click install grants an agent write access to your active music projects; work on COPIES/BACKUPS and treat destructive actions with caution. REQUIRED one-time operator setup (uvx install does NOT ship the repo's enable_reapy.py, and uvx does not install python-reapy into REAPER's Python, so use reapy's own canonical setup): SEPARATELY `pip install python-reapy`, then with REAPER OPEN run `python -c "import reapy; reapy.configure_reaper()"` (installs the reapy bridge into REAPER and enables the distant API — per the python-reapy README/install guide), then restart REAPER. The host-exe probe detects a REAPER install, NOT whether the distant API is configured, so complete this before first use. MATURITY: Alpha (pyproject Development Status :: 3 - Alpha; thin tests upstream) — offered to try, not all 58 tools are equally battle-tested. disabled-until-probe: enables when uvx is on PATH AND a host REAPER install is detected via the Windows glob C:\Program Files*\REAPER*\reaper.exe (the leading Files* covers BOTH the 64-bit C:\Program Files and the 32-bit C:\Program Files (x86) install roots; the default x64 install lands at C:\Program Files\REAPER (x64)\reaper.exe; the trailing-* on REAPER matches the version-suffixed variants). REQUIRES Python 3.10+ and uv on PATH plus a host REAPER install. macOS (/Applications/REAPER*.app) and Linux REAPER paths are NOT covered in this batch — file_globs[] entries are AND-semantics and cannot OR a second install root (same limit as the Ableton row), so a macOS/Linux probe is a follow-up.

entries.name: Grafana MCP server (official)
entries.summary: Drive a Grafana server from an AI client -- search and read dashboards, query Prometheus/Loki/other datasources, manage alerting and incidents, render panel images, and more. OFFICIAL Grafana server (grafana/mcp-grafana, Apache-2.0), pinned to release v0.17.0. The PyPI package mcp-grafana==0.17.0 is a thin Python wheel that bundles the per-platform Go server binary (win/linux/darwin x64+arm64), run via uvx. STDIO by design: the Go binary's default transport is stdio (this row passes -t stdio explicitly to pin it); the SSE / streamable-http modes are opt-in (-t sse / -t streamable-http) and even then bind localhost:8000 (loopback, not 0.0.0.0), so there is no LAN surface. CONFIG BURDEN: this row drives a Grafana SERVER you already run -- set GRAFANA_URL to your instance (defaults to http://localhost:3000) and supply a Grafana service-account token. The token is wired to the mcphub vault as GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN = secret:grafana_service_account_token (GRAFANA_API_KEY is the deprecated old env name -- the row uses the current GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN). The token is the OPTIONAL-secret posture (not a required_secrets install gate): the server starts without it (auth is enforced per-tool-call at the Grafana API), and read-only tools work against an anonymous-access instance, so a one-click install is not hard-blocked. Supply the token only through the hub vault, never as plaintext. disabled-until-probe: enables when uvx is on PATH.

entries.name: Tableau MCP server (official)
entries.summary: Query and explore your Tableau Server / Tableau Cloud from an AI client -- list and read published data sources, run VizQL queries, browse workbooks, and more. OFFICIAL Tableau server (tableau/tableau-mcp, Apache-2.0), the npm package @tableau/mcp-server pinned to v2.18.1 and run via npx (a Node launcher around build/index.js). NODE REQUIREMENT: @tableau/mcp-server@2.18.1 declares engines.node >= 22.7.5 -- the install probe cannot version-check node, so on a host with an older node (e.g. 20.x) the install completes but the daemon fails at spawn with a clear node-version error. Ensure Node 22.7.5+ is on PATH before installing. STDIO by default: the entry selects stdio unless TRANSPORT=http is set (this row sets no TRANSPORT, so it is stdio); the opt-in http mode binds all interfaces (.listen(port) with no host) and additionally requires OAUTH_ISSUER -- NOT used by this row. REQUIRED config + auth (install BLOCKS until all are set in the mcphub vault): the server hard-exits on startup without SERVER / PAT_NAME / PAT_VALUE, and there is no required-non-secret-config mechanism, so the Tableau instance URL is routed through the required_secrets gate as SERVER = secret:tableau_server_url alongside the PAT (PAT_NAME = secret:tableau_pat_name + PAT_VALUE = secret:tableau_pat_value). This prevents a one-click install from silently shipping a placeholder URL as the live default. SITE_NAME stays an editable literal (empty default = the Default site on Tableau Server; Tableau Cloud needs the site's content URL). Supply the URL + PAT only through the hub vault, never as plaintext.

entries.name: Adobe Photoshop MCP server
entries.summary: Drive Adobe Photoshop from an AI client -- create/open/save documents, add text and solid-color layers, run actions, and inspect the active document -- via the photoshop-python-api COM bridge. Community server loonghao/photoshop-python-api-mcp-server (Python, MIT), published to PyPI as photoshop-mcp-server and pinned to v0.1.11, run via uvx with the version pinned. WINDOWS-ONLY COM: the server talks to a running Photoshop over Windows COM (win32com via pywin32) -- there is NO socket, NO network listener, and NO manual plugin to install (unlike the DAW rows). It is stdio + COM, so loopback-clean by construction. The Adobe classifier and the COM dependency are Windows-only, so the install_probe ARCH-GATES on platforms: [windows/amd64]; on any other OS the row stays inert. AUTO-DETECTS THE INSTALLED PHOTOSHOP: v0.1.11's COM adapter constructs the Photoshop application with no version argument (Session()/Application()), so it connects to whichever Photoshop the COM ProgID resolves to -- the README's PS_VERSION env var is NOT consumed by this pinned version, so the row sets no PS_VERSION (a hardcoded year would be inert and misleading). The probe glob is therefore VERSION-AGNOSTIC -- REQUIRES a host Adobe Photoshop install detected via C:\Program Files\Adobe\Adobe Photoshop *\Photoshop.exe (the trailing * matches any year-versioned install root, e.g. Adobe Photoshop 2024 / 2025), which now correctly matches the auto-detect behavior for any installed version. Photoshop must be RUNNING for tools to act on a document; the host-exe probe detects the install, not whether Photoshop is open. REQUIRES Python 3.10+ and uv on PATH (the README recommends the --python 3.10 pin, which uv satisfies by fetching a managed CPython 3.10 if needed).

entries.name: Zotero MCP server
entries.summary: Search and read your Zotero reference library from an AI client -- look up items, collections, tags, notes, and full-text content. Community server kujenga/zotero-mcp (Python, MIT), published to PyPI as zotero-mcp and pinned to v0.1.6, run via uvx. LOOPBACK-CLEAN: the server is stdio (default transport stdio; --transport sse is opt-in and not used) and, with ZOTERO_LOCAL=true, acts as a CLIENT to the Zotero desktop application's OWN built-in local API at http://localhost:23119 (verified loopback in the pyzotero dependency) -- NO third-party add-on, NO network listener opened by this server. ZOTERO_LOCAL=true is a literal config value (not a secret), and in local mode ZOTERO_API_KEY / ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID are NOT required, so this is a clean no-secret row. To enable the local API, run the Zotero 7 desktop app with the local API turned on (Settings -> Advanced). disabled-until-probe: enables when uvx is on PATH; REQUIRES Python 3.11+ and uv plus the Zotero desktop app running for live queries.

entries.name: Metabase MCP server
entries.summary: Query and explore your Metabase BI instance from an AI client -- run questions/cards, browse databases and dashboards, and export card results as CSV/JSON. Community server (NOT official) easecloudio/mcp-metabase-server (Node, MIT), the npm package @easecloudio/mcp-metabase-server pinned to v1.3.0 and run via npx. LOOPBACK-CLEAN: the server uses StdioServerTransport only -- no port bind, no 0.0.0.0, no HTTP listener. READ-ONLY BY DEFAULT: this row sets TOOL_MODE=read (the upstream non-destructive tool set) so a one-click install cannot create/update/delete dashboards, cards, databases, or users; the operator opts into the destructive surface explicitly by editing the manifest to TOOL_MODE=all (everything) or TOOL_MODE=write (incl. create/update/delete). Omitting TOOL_MODE would default upstream to `all`, so the row pins `read`. REQUIRED config + auth (install BLOCKS until both are set in the mcphub vault): the server hard-exits on startup without METABASE_URL, and there is no required-non-secret-config mechanism, so the instance URL is routed through the required_secrets gate as METABASE_URL = secret:metabase_url alongside the API key METABASE_API_KEY = secret:metabase_api_key. This prevents a one-click install from silently shipping a placeholder URL as the live default -- every install must supply the real instance URL + key first. Supply both only through the hub vault, never as plaintext.

entries.name: Jupyter MCP server
entries.summary: Drive a running Jupyter (JupyterLab / Jupyter Server) from an AI client -- list and edit notebook cells, execute code, read outputs, and manage kernels. Community server datalayer/jupyter-mcp-server (Python, BSD-3-Clause), published to PyPI as jupyter-mcp-server and pinned to v1.0.2, run via uvx. STDIO-PINNED: the CLI's default transport is stdio, and this row passes --transport stdio EXPLICITLY to pin it -- the alternative streamable-http mode binds host=0.0.0.0 (all interfaces, LAN-reachable) and is NOT used. REQUIRES a RUNNING Jupyter server: set JUPYTER_URL to its URL (defaults to http://localhost:8888) and supply the Jupyter token wired to the mcphub vault as JUPYTER_TOKEN = secret:jupyter_token. The token is the OPTIONAL-secret posture (not a required_secrets gate): the MCP server starts without a reachable Jupyter (it connects lazily), so a one-click install is not hard-blocked, but the tools need the running Jupyter + token to work. The MCP_TOKEN auth knob only applies to the unused streamable-http standalone mode. Supply the token only through the hub vault, never as plaintext. disabled-until-probe: enables when uvx is on PATH (Python 3.10+, uv).

entries.name: RMCP -- R statistics MCP server
entries.summary: Run R statistical analysis from an AI client -- 52 tools spanning regression, hypothesis testing, time series, and more -- driven through Rscript on PATH. Community server (Python, MIT) published to PyPI as rmcp and pinned to v0.8.1, run via uvx. PROVENANCE: the PyPI rmcp project_urls point to github.com/finite-sample/rmcp (Gaurav Sood), so the vendored_source pins that repo; v0.8.1 has no git tag, so the pin is the HEAD commit that ships version 0.8.1 in its pyproject. STDIO-PINNED: this row runs the `start` subcommand, which is the stdio transport -- the `serve-http --host 0.0.0.0` mode is the opt-in non-default (binds all interfaces, needs the http extras) and is NOT used; plain `start` does not even install the HTTP deps. No secret and no required env. REQUIRES R on PATH (the tools shell out to Rscript); the server starts and degrades gracefully WITHOUT R (it logs a warning and R-dependent tools fail at call time), so the install_probe gates only on uvx -- a host that installs R later does not need to re-probe. disabled-until-probe: enables when uvx is on PATH (Python 3.11+, uv); install R 4.4.0+ separately for the analysis tools.

entries.name: Obsidian MCP server
entries.summary: Read, search, and edit your Obsidian vault from an AI client -- list files, read/append/patch notes, full-text and JsonLogic search, and manage the periodic-note daily journal -- via Obsidian's Local REST API community plugin. Community server MarkusPfundstein/mcp-obsidian (Python, MIT), published to PyPI as mcp-obsidian and pinned to v0.2.2, run via uvx. LOOPBACK-CLEAN: the MCP server is stdio (mcp.server.stdio) and acts as a CLIENT to the plugin's local API at https://127.0.0.1:27124 (verified loopback default host=127.0.0.1 in obsidian.py) -- it opens NO network listener of its own. PREREQUISITE (REQUIRED, operator-side): the MCP server does NOT talk to Obsidian directly -- it talks to the 'Local REST API' Obsidian COMMUNITY PLUGIN, which you must install once from Obsidian's in-app community-plugin store (Settings -> Community plugins -> Browse -> 'Local REST API') and ENABLE; the plugin then binds 127.0.0.1 and mints the API key you store below. The host-exe probe is not applicable (no separate Obsidian binary on PATH and the gate is the plugin + key), so this row gates on the required secret. Origin must be RUNNING for tools to act; the host-exe probe detects the install, not whether Origin is open. REQUIRES Python + uv on PATH. MATURITY CAVEAT: LOW-maturity, Alpha (Development Status :: 3 - Alpha; ~21 GitHub stars at time of curation, v0.1.0 single release) -- offered to try, verify each operation before relying on it. disabled-until-probe: enables only when uvx AND a host Origin install are present on a windows/amd64 host.

Search itself is keyless (the Semantic Scholar API works at the shared public rate limit -- no secret). Requires Python + uv on PATH.
docs_only.manual_install: Add it directly to your MCP client after reviewing the destructive-tool caveat. Pinned, project-isolated launch: `uv run --no-project --with scholar-search-mcp==0.1.3 python -m scholar_search_mcp` -- the --no-project flag avoids discovering an ambient Python project/workspace (a global daemon inherits the supervisor cwd; a stray pyproject.toml with an incompatible requires-python would otherwise break the server). Enable the backends with env SCHOLAR_SEARCH_ENABLE_SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR=true and SCHOLAR_SEARCH_ENABLE_ARXIV=true. DESTRUCTIVE-TOOL CAVEAT: this server exposes `download_arxiv_source`, which extracts an arXiv paper's LaTeX/source bundle under a caller-supplied output_dir and DELETES/overwrites <output_dir>/<arxiv_id> before fetching -- an agent that supplies a sensitive output_dir (e.g. ~ or ~/.ssh) could wipe files there even if the download fails. Only ever pass a safe, dedicated output_dir, Setting env SCHOLAR_ARXIV_SOURCE_DIR only changes the DEFAULT base used when a call OMITS output_dir; it does NOT constrain an explicit output_dir an agent supplies, so it is not a safety gate. Requires Python + uv on PATH.
